content: Public bodies in the UK spent £3.4bn on private consultants in 2023-24, a 62% increase from 2019-20, with spending remaining high after the pandemic. Labour’s government aims to halve this expenditure but has already awarded new contracts worth nearly £650m, including a £223m deal with KPMG for civil service training. Critics argue that relying on consultants is ineffective, as they often lack the time to understand complex organizations deeply. Is there anything else I can help with?
